source.title: Sparse autoencoders reveal selective remapping of visual concepts during adaptation
source.authors: Hyesu Lim; Jin-Ho Choi; Jaegul Choo; Steffen Schneider

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether an overcomplete SAE recovers interpretable, functionally relevant features in a CLIP vision transformer, extending evidence about dictionary features to a vision model rather than testing the original toy-network setup or an LLM.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE reconstruction and feature-masking outcomes relevant to recoverable sparse features. The adaptation results about remapping concepts to task classes do not directly test feature-capacity competition or superposition geometry.
record.test_reason: The study uses an SAE as an interpretability tool on CLIP ViT-B/16 to study prompt-based adaptation. Its quantitative results validate the tool (reconstruction accuracy, latent-masking ablations) and analyse adaptation; they do not measure whether superposition or polysemanticity holds. V4 names LLMs, and this is a vision encoder, so the rows do not bear on V4 as stated. The finding that an SAE recovers class-discriminative sparse latents in a ViT is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that PatchSAE extracts interpretable, spatially localized concepts from CLIP ViT and that its latents carry class-discriminative information. Most prompt-adaptation (MaPLe) gains come from remapping concepts already present to task classes, with EuroSAT the one task showing non-negligible newly activated or suppressed concepts.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and evaluates a sparse autoencoder on CLIP vision-transformer activations and tests feature masking in classification; it does not use the original toy-network feature-generation and geometry experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that deeper hook layers yield semantically richer SAE latents than shallower layers. For the adaptation analysis, outcomes vary by dataset; EuroSAT shows more notable changes in feature activation than most tested tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: A 64x-expansion SAE on layer-11 residual stream of CLIP ViT-B/16 retains most zero-shot ImageNet accuracy (64.82% vs 68.25%). Ablating per-class top latents degrades accuracy, while random or dataset-level latents have marginal effect. Many latents are qualitatively interpretable, and deeper layers give semantically richer latents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision transformers (CLIP ViT) contain sparse, class-relevant features that an SAE can recover (V4 extended beyond LLMs).

record.problems: The evidence concerns one CLIP vision encoder and a particular SAE design; the paper does not establish feature completeness, stability, or canonicality, nor test superposition geometry or capacity pressure. Interpretability is evaluated substantially through qualitative examples, and no uncertainty estimates are reported for the classification results.
record.rows_left_out: The study reports additional layer, dataset-transfer, adaptation, and base/novel classification analyses. These were not included because they do not directly measure the claim versions about superposition, capacity competition, canonical dictionary units, or feature dimensionality.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition, or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity are examined.
No LLMs. Neuron-level polysemanticity or feature spread is not measured; polysemanticity is only asserted in the background.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality are not tested. Uninterpretable high-entropy latents are noted only qualitatively.
Dimensionality of features is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: This is an applied SAE/adaptation paper. Superposition is invoked only in related work as motivation. The reader's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels were dropped: the subject is a vision encoder rather than an LLM, and the rows are validations of the authors' own tool and selection comparisons. If V4 is broadened to transformer models generally, R1 and R3 could be relinked as weak T3 evidence, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, overlap geometry, and regular geometric arrangements.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The study tests SAE-recoverable features in a CLIP vision encoder, not LLMs or features spread across individual neurons.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features are not established.
The study uses linear SAE latent directions but does not test whether underlying model features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the intermediate representation with the SAE reconstruction using the identity mask over all 49,152 latents.
rows.note: The authors describe this as recovering the original performance with small reconstruction errors, although the reported accuracy is lower.
rows.check: This validates the study's own SAE: identity-mask reconstruction gives 64.82% vs 68.25% original. The system is a CLIP vision encoder, not an LLM as V4 names. It shows reconstruction fidelity, not superposition.

rows.subject: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Set the SAE latent mask to all zeros before decoding.
rows.note: The paper says the all-zero mask removes all relevant information.
rows.check: The all-zero mask giving 0.1% is a trivial sanity check of the tool. It cannot show any version's effect.

rows.subject: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Masked SAE latents selected as the top class-activating latents; the number retained or ablated was varied.
rows.value: The paper reports a clear improvement or degradation as the number of active SAE latents is increased or decreased, respectively.
rows.note: The text does not give the separate plotted values for each k.
rows.check: This is a selection-based ablation of the study's own method; no values are stated in the text. It shows class-relevant latents matter for classification, not superposition, and the system is a vision model.

rows.subject: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Ablated randomly selected SAE latent indices, using the same number of indices as the compared selection.
rows.value: No significant effect until a sufficient number of latents was used.
rows.note: The paper does not specify the threshold for a sufficient number in the text.
rows.check: Control for R3 (random latents). This compares selection methods within the study's own method, and the threshold is unstated.

rows.subject: OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Ablated dataset-level representative latents, selected for frequent activation across classes in the dataset.
rows.value: The paper reports marginal or no impact for dataset-level selections.
rows.note: The text does not give separate accuracy values for each k.
rows.check: Dataset-level selection comparator. This compares selection methods within the tool; it is not a measure of any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CLIP ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1K, using the trained PatchSAE
reader_labels.reason: The SAE reconstruction retains substantial classification performance, and masking its class-relevant latents changes accuracy while the all-zero mask removes relevant information (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The full SAE reconstruction does not match the original accuracy, and random or dataset-level selections have little effect compared with per-class selections; evidence is for selective, functionally relevant SAE latents, not a complete account of model features (R1, R4, R5).
